page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State Walli's formula for odd n
steps.margin_note: First mark. n=7 is odd, so no π/2 factor appears.
steps.memory_tip: The sinⁿx and cosⁿx odd-n formulas have the identical shape — only the value of n changes.
lines: When n is odd, ∫₀^(π/2) sinⁿx dx
steps.why: For an odd power of sin, Walli's formula uses the same descending-product pattern as the cosine version, ending at 2 on top and 3 on the bottom with no π/2 factor.
common_mistakes: Using the even-n version of the formula for this odd n=7 case.
Confusing this with the cos¹¹x formula from the previous answer, which has five terms rather than three.

steps.label: Substitute n=7 and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 48/105 reduces to 16/35 by dividing both by 3.
steps.memory_tip: For n=7 there are exactly three descending terms in each product.
steps.why: Substituting n=7 gives the three-term descending product 6·4·2=48 over 7·5·3=105, which simplifies to 16/35 after dividing by the common factor 3.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as the unsimplified fraction 48/105 instead of reducing it to 16/35.
Missing a term in the three-term product.
